text: A king escape available in the diagram makes the problem easy to solve.
A try refuted by a king move is pretty bad.
The same refutation for several thematic tries is bad.
Every piece should take part in the mates; the key piece is forgivable.
No obvious Black defence without an answer, or the key becomes trivial.
Simple defences (pawn moves opening lines for the king) defend against anything and help the solver; heavy pieces moving and leaving squares are better.
Economy and an airy position are valued, but aesthetics yield to content as ideas get richer.
A natural, game-like look adds points.
Long moves, paradoxes, thematic play and geometric manoeuvres are valued; more so when doubled or tripled.
Too simple plus big flaws is not worth it, even if economical.
source: E. Bourd s1 (on the Kh6 Bristol miniature)
